newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT- "Protect our rugby tradition"- Canty coach.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT- "Protect our rugby tradition"- Canty coach.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Oct 16 - Canterbury coach Vance Stewart on Wednesday appealed to the country's rugby hierachy to defend the traditions of New Zealand rugby, NZPA reports.
Stewart said he had some concerns for the direction the game was taking in Canterbury and possibly in other parts of New Zealand.
Canterbury play Counties on Saturday in the NPC first division semifinals in a match which could be Stewart's penultimate or last game as coach.
"We have to be careful that the provinces don't become overly focused on the Super 12," Stewart said today.
"There is still provincial rugby out there, supporting club and junior rugby. That should still be our primary objective. We shouldn't forget that at the expense of Super 12 rugby.
"We must not drift away from the traditions of New Zealand rugby and the Super 12 should be dealt with by a separate company," he told NZPA.
Stewart said the game should not drift away from the grassroots which were at risk of being eroded.

"We don't want to lose our traditions which have served us so well. Remember our rugby is still an amateur game and we still need to maintain the stepping stone process from schoolboy rugby and continue to develop that."
Rugby went professional for the elite players last year so they could be paid enough money to stop them from being lost to league or to overseas teams.
But provinces like Canterbury were not getting any more fans through the gates and there was insufficient money left for them to protect their NPC players.
There are concerns some provinces are pouring too many resources into the Super 12 instead of fostering the game from the bottom up.
Meanwhile, Stewart, a former All Blacks lock, bows out this month after seven years with Canterbury, three with the colts team and four as the top coach.
His side reached the NPC semifinals in 1994, held the Ranfurly Shield for most of last season and made the NPC semifinals this year.
He has brought to prominence such players as Angus Gardiner, Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall, Mark Mayerhofler and Tabai Matson.
The latter part of this year has been the most difficult period of Stewart's coaching career.
"We achieved our goals this season and I am disappointed that after seven years there has been no acknowledgement from the union," he said.
